initial_observation.encounter_context: admitted to Rasoul Akram Social Security Hospital in Rasht City, Guilan Province, North of Iran, owing to fever and chills
initial_observation.first_contact_summary: He was a nonsmoker and nondiabetic and had no history of hypertension, connective tissue disorders, congenital diseases, or any other known medical conditions. There was also no personal or family history of cardiovascular diseases, connective tissue disorders, hypertension, or other predisposing factors. The patient’s vital signs upon admission were as follows: blood pressure, 100/60 mmHg; heart rate, 100 beats per minute; temperature, 38 °C; respiratory rate, 22 breaths per minute. First of all, he was visited by an infectious disease specialist, and lab tests were sent for analysis. He was treated with vancomycin and meropenem antibiotics.

In the hospital, the patient experienced facial nerve palsy, diplopia, dysarthria, and seizures.

The National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score was 8, with the following components: visual field defect (homonymous hemianopia), 2; facial palsy, 3; ataxia, 1; speech disturbance (dysarthria or aphasia), 1.
A magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scan was performed, revealing multiple cortical infarcts in the brain (Fig. 1).

Owing to multiple cortical infarcts found on a brain MRI, a consultation with a cardiologist was requested, and the patient underwent cardiac echocardiography. The echocardiography revealed an aortic aneurysm with a diameter of 7.7 cm.

To confirm the diagnosis and rule out endocarditis, the patient then underwent transesophageal echocardiography (TEE). During the TEE, the following findings were reported: ejection fraction (EF) of 40–45%; very severe aortic aneurysm (AI); dilated aortic aneurysm measuring 6.9 cm; mild mitral regurgitation (MR); minimal tricuspid regurgitation (TR); mild pulmonary insufficiency (PI); pulmonary artery pressure (PAP) of 50 mm/Hg; severe left ventricle enlargement measuring 136 cm/m2 with mild systolic dysfunction; a large (1.1 cm) semi-mobile mass on the arterial side of the noncoronary cusp (NCC) mostly resembling vegetation; very severe aortic regurgitation (AR), aneurysmal aortic root (annulus, 3.1 cm; sinus of valsalva (SOV), 4.2 cm; effacement of sinotubular junction (STJ)); aneurysmal dilation of the ascending aorta with the proximal portion measuring 6.8 cm and the distal portion measuring 3.9 cm; a visible linear flap of aortic dissection originating about 1.3 cm after the aortic valve (AV); the dissecting flap appearing thickened and infected; and mild circumferential pericardial effusion (5 mm around all cardiac chambers).

Unfortunately, our center did not have the necessary facilities for Bentall surgery, so the patient was transferred to Imam Khomeini Hospital Complex in Tehran, the capital of Iran. Subsequently, 2 days later, the patient underwent the Bentall procedure. During the surgery, the aortic valve, ascending aorta, and its root were replaced with a mechanical composite graft (Carbomedics), size 27.

After the surgery, the patient was admitted to the cardiac intensive care unit (ICU) and started on warfarin. Once the chest drainage tubes were removed, the patient was transferred to the infectious ward where he continued antibiotic therapy with ciprofloxacin, ampicillin/sulbactam, and vancomycin.

The lab tests conducted during discharge showed the following results: white blood cells (WBCs), 4000 × 103 UL; platelets (PLTs), 327,000 × 103 UL; International Normalized Ratio (INR), 2.6; sodium (Na), 145 mEq/L; creatinine (Cr), 0.8 mg/dL; hemoglobin (HB), 9.10mg/dL; and potassium (K), 3.7 mEq/L.

At the first follow-up visit in our neurology clinic, the patient was clinically re-evaluated. The NIHSS score had decreased to 3, with the following findings: visual field defect improved to 1; facial palsy improved to 1; speech disturbance remained at 1; and ataxia completely resolved.

hidden_reference.final_diagnosis_verbatim: According to the TEE report, which indicated endocarditis, aortic aneurysm, and aortic dissection, the patient was in need of emergent cardiac surgery (Bentall surgery).
